text:
incident-bot: SEV2 ALERT: gpu-pool-usw2 autoscaler hit maxNodes=48; scheduler backlog growing. metric: PendingPods=187, QueueDepth=1400, PodEvictions=12. Autoscaler state: NotScaling(ceiling_reached). IncidentID=INC-2026-33065

alejandro: saw the alert, jumping in. which pools exactly? any affected customer-facing routes?

priya: gpu-pool-usw2 (g4/g5 mix). traffic spike from batch embedder + a large customer inference job. some hosted customers seeing 5-15s extra latency, and a few 503s. telemetry: error_rate by route shows /v1/generate bump from 0.3% -> 2.8% in last 4m.

sam: Confirming pending pods stuck in Pending->Unschedulable: "0/48 nodes available: insufficient gpu, node(s) had taint". kube-scheduler logs show scheduling failures due to gpuAllocatable exhaustion.

infra-nick: autoscaler config: cluster-autoscaler min=8 max=48 for gpu-pool-usw2. We hit maxNodes. Cloud quota for GPU cores is at limit for this account in us-west-2; requests for more nodes are blocked by provider.

sre-maya: immediate mitigation options: 1) manual temporary node pool increase (requires quota request or using a spare subscription) 2) evict low-priority batch jobs (preemptible buckets) 3) route a fraction of traffic to eu-west-1 fallback region 4) enable autoscaler fallback to smaller model variant. Which is fastest?

alejandro: priority is keep customer-facing traffic healthy. Start with 2 and 3 now. Priya, can you identify batch jobs to evict? Sam, can you open a quick route-switch PR or toggle?

priya: listing jobs to evict now. matching label app=batch-embedder and priorityClass=low. Estimated reclaim ~9 GPUs if we evict active jobs: 6 long-running embeddings + 2 ephemeral preprocessors. Command: ```kubectl get pods -l app=batch-embedder -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Running``` 

sam: I can flip routing via the traffic-router feature flag. Will route 20% traffic to eu-west-1 blue pool. Pushing change in 30s. Notifying ops-oncall before change.

ops-oncall: ack, will monitor RUM and error budget. If failures continue escalate to customer-success for outbound comms.

incident-bot: action logged: runbook "gpu-pool-saturation" step 2 executed by priya at 3306543285.

priya: evicted low-priority pods: 8 pods removed, reclaimed 10 GPUs, queueDepth down from 1400 -> 920, PendingPods -> 112. Affected batch jobs will restart on fallback pools when capacity returns.

sam: routing change done. 20% traffic now hitting eu-west-1. Initial metrics: latency on eu-west-1 higher by ~40ms but error_rate there is stable. Global /v1/generate error_rate down to 1.1% from 2.8%.

infra-nick: cloud quota request for more GPUs already submitted but provider ETA ~4-6 hours. We can also spin up a temporary nodepool in a different account (requires manual credentialing). Alejandro, do you want us to request immediate manual cap raise from infra owners for this pool? That would involve increasing maxNodes to 64 and invoking provider quota escalation.

alejandro: yes, request a manual cap raise. Priya and Sam keep monitoring. Nick, coordinate with platform-ops to get the manual bump. If provider refuses, we'll convert spare compute from fallbacks to dedicated for customers impacted. I approve emergency increase to maxNodes=64 for gpu-pool-usw2.

infra-nick: starting manual cap raise: running terraform apply on infra-gpu-usw2 (plan shows change: aws_autoscaling_group.gpu-usw2.max_size: 48 -> 64). Command snippet: ```TF_VAR_region=us-west-2 terraform apply -target=module.gpu_pool.aws_autoscaling_group.gpu-usw2 -auto-approve``` 

sre-maya: note: after node increase, kubelet will need ~2-3m/node to register and then CA will scale pending pods. Expect full recovery ~15-25m if nodes come up continuously.

incident-bot: approval recorded: alejandro approved emergency autoscaler max increase to 64 at 3306543348.

infra-nick: TF apply started. Monitoring cloud console: new capacity provisioning in progress, instances launching.

priya: customer-impact note for CS: ~10 hosted customers experienced degraded latency; ~3 customers saw 503s for <10 minutes during peak. We're routing traffic and reclaimed some capacity; pursuing manual cap raise.

sam: small follow-up: toggled model fallback for particularly noisy tenant (tenant-id: T-997) to v2-small for the next 30m. This reduced their token-per-request footprint and prevented further queue spikes.

sre-maya: pods starting to schedule on new nodes. PendingPods -> 34, QueueDepth -> 210. Token throughput returning to baseline.

incident-bot: TF apply completed; autoscaler maxNodes=64 applied at 3306543430. Instances registered: +16 nodes reported by cloud provider.

infra-nick: kube nodes registered: +14 GPU nodes became Ready (2 still provisioning). CA started scale-down checks. All previously Pending pods are now scheduling.

alejandro: thanks team. Good fast mitigations. Priya please prepare a brief post-incident note for CS: timeline, customer impact, mitigation steps, and follow-ups (request quota increase with provider and add overflow pool).

priya: on it. Draft will include: root cause = sudden concurrent large batch embedder + regression from customer script; mitigations = evict low-priority jobs, route 20% to eu-west-1, manual cap raise to 64, temporary model fallback for heavy tenant; follow-ups = request permanent quota increase, add autoscaler policy to permit cross-region spillover, add alert for PendingPods>50 sustained for 5m.

ops-oncall: I'm taking the handoff for next 2 hours to watch for regressions. Summary for next oncall: restored capacity, autoscaler max temporarily 64 (pending quota change), monitor PendingPods, QueueDepth, /v1/generate error_rate.

alejandro: handing to ops-oncall. If anything degrades, call me. Closing this thread after we confirm postmortem and provider quota decision. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated). Active severity downgraded to REDUCED at 3306543470. Follow-up task created: FT-2026-58 (quota-request + add overflow pool)."
